summary.text: Amish Shah is an emergency-medicine physician and the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. He served in the Arizona House of Representatives from 2019 to 2024 and was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024, losing to Rep. David Schweikert. His campaign website says he has focused on teacher pay, small businesses, and public health and safety.

paragraphs.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, to parents who immigrated from India in the 1960s, according to Wikipedia. Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Northwestern University in 1997, an M.D. from Northwestern University in 2001, and a master's in public health from the University of California, Berkeley in 2003.

Completed a residency in emergency medicine in New York City and joined the faculty of Mount Sinai Medical Center, where he worked on a project to improve player safety in the NFL. He was a team physician for the New York Jets for five seasons, then moved to Arizona for a sports medicine fellowship at the University of Arizona.

Worked as an attending physician with Mayo Clinic, Dignity Health, and IASIS Healthcare, and as chief medical officer of Urgent Consult; as of 2023 he was an emergency physician at Mayo Clinic Arizona.

Entered politics in 2018, winning one of two seats in Arizona's 24th legislative district after defeating incumbent Rep. Ken Clark and others in the Democratic primary. He was sworn into the Arizona House on January 14, 2019.

Served in the Arizona House of Representatives, District 24 (2019-2023) and, after redistricting, District 5 (2023-2024), re-elected in 2020 and 2022. His sponsored bills focused largely on health care, including prior-authorization forms, emergency medical transport, and physician peer support.
Won a six-candidate Democratic primary for Arizona's 1st Congressional District in 2024 with 23.5% of the vote, then lost the general election to incumbent Rep. David Schweikert 51.9%-48.1%.
Announced a second run for the seat in May 2025 and won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 39.4% of the vote, ahead of Marlene Galan-Woods (34.4%), Jonathan Treble, and Rick McCartney.
According to his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia, he has had a record of working across party lines, and had "more bills signed into law than any Arizona Democrat in the last decade."
